companies.name: NVIDIA
companies.description: Accelerated computing, from AI infrastructure to graphics.

evidence.title: How NVIDIA makes money
evidence.summary: NVIDIA sells accelerated computing platforms: chips, networking, systems and software. Its reported segments are Compute & Networking and Graphics.
evidence.question: Who buys these platforms, and what problem do they solve?
evidence.keywords: revenue business money gpu chips graphics platform segments doanh thu kiem tien

evidence.title: The demand behind the story
evidence.summary: The filing attributes Data Center growth to demand for accelerated computing and AI. Historical demand does not establish future growth or stock returns.
evidence.question: What would you need to see to believe demand can continue?
evidence.keywords: growth demand ai datacenter data center revenue tang truong nhu cau

evidence.title: A supply chain to understand
evidence.summary: NVIDIA relies on outside suppliers for wafer fabrication, assembly, testing and packaging. Supply constraints or disruptions can affect its ability to deliver products.
evidence.question: How could a supplier disruption affect the business?
evidence.keywords: risk supply chain manufacturing supplier fabrication packaging rui ro cung ung

evidence.title: Export restrictions
evidence.summary: The company describes export controls as a constraint on sales to certain markets, including China. Changes can affect demand, distribution and its competitive position.
evidence.question: Which part of this risk is documented, and what remains uncertain?
evidence.keywords: risk export restrictions controls china regulation xuat khau trung quoc

revenueMix.label: Data Center
revenueMix.explanation: Computing and networking for data centers, including AI workloads.

revenueMix.label: Other markets
revenueMix.explanation: Professional visualization, automotive, OEM and other markets combined.

financials.sourceSection: Consolidated Statements of Income; Note 16 — Revenue by End Market

companies.name: Microsoft
companies.description: Productivity software, cloud infrastructure and personal computing.

evidence.title: How Microsoft makes money
evidence.summary: Microsoft reports Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. Products span Microsoft 365, Azure, Windows, gaming and other services.
evidence.question: How do subscriptions differ from one-time product sales?
evidence.keywords: revenue business money cloud azure software subscriptions segments doanh thu kiem tien

evidence.title: Cloud and AI demand
evidence.summary: Microsoft describes cloud and AI services as growth areas. The report also discusses investment in infrastructure needed to support these services.
evidence.question: How would you distinguish demand growth from profitable growth?
evidence.keywords: growth demand ai cloud azure infrastructure investment tang truong nhu cau

evidence.title: Competition across the stack
evidence.summary: Azure competes with other cloud providers and open-source offerings. Microsoft's AI competitors include hyperscalers and emerging providers, some of which are also partners.
evidence.question: What evidence would help you assess a durable advantage?
evidence.keywords: risk competition competitors cloud azure open source rui ro canh tranh

evidence.title: Security and trust
evidence.summary: The report identifies cybersecurity threats and service disruption as business risks. Failures can affect customers, reputation and operations.
evidence.question: How might a loss of customer trust affect recurring business?
evidence.keywords: risk security cybersecurity trust disruption customers rui ro bao mat

revenueMix.label: Productivity & Business
revenueMix.explanation: Microsoft 365, LinkedIn and Dynamics; report name: Productivity and Business Processes.

revenueMix.label: Intelligent Cloud
revenueMix.explanation: Server products, Azure and enterprise services.

revenueMix.label: Personal Computing
revenueMix.explanation: Windows, devices, gaming and search; report name: More Personal Computing.

companies.name: Apple
companies.description: Devices and services built around an integrated ecosystem.

evidence.title: How Apple makes money
evidence.summary: Apple sells iPhone, Mac, iPad, wearables and accessories, alongside services including digital content, cloud services, payment services and advertising.
evidence.question: How are product revenue and services revenue different?
evidence.keywords: revenue business money iphone services products devices doanh thu kiem tien

evidence.title: Products and services
evidence.summary: Apple's product and services offerings are linked through its ecosystem. Its report discusses the importance of introducing products and services that appeal to customers.
evidence.question: What evidence would show customers want the next generation?
evidence.keywords: growth demand ecosystem products services innovation customers tang truong nhu cau

evidence.title: Manufacturing dependencies
evidence.summary: Apple relies on outsourcing partners for manufacturing and logistics, many outside the U.S. It also relies on single-source partners for many components.
evidence.question: How could this dependence affect product availability?
evidence.keywords: risk supply chain manufacturing outsourcing partners components rui ro cung ung

evidence.title: Competition and product transitions
evidence.summary: The company describes intense competition and risks around product introductions and transitions. An unsuccessful transition can affect its business and financial results.
evidence.question: What would challenge the idea that a familiar brand is always a safe investment?
evidence.keywords: risk competition transitions innovation products rui ro canh tranh

revenueMix.label: Services
revenueMix.explanation: Services including advertising, the App Store and cloud services.

revenueMix.label: Other products
revenueMix.explanation: Mac, iPad, Wearables, Home and Accessories combined.

financials.sourceSection: Consolidated Statements of Operations; Note 2 — Revenue
